digest.component_or_area: code review criteria language (tests and error-handling)
propositions: A check producing an ABSENCE assertion (empty output, negative grep, no collection) derived from subprocess/file/network capture has fail-open risk if producer liveness is not verified, making its pass result indistinguishable from the producer never running.

The fail-open defect mirrors: a broken instrument can produce a confident FAIL result for a reason other than the verified condition (e.g., wrong input to git show), making false alarms equally problematic as false passes.

Code-review criterion language for fail-open checks must cover both test-oracle population (tests criterion: absence assertions on subprocess output, grep-based pass/fail signals) and shipped-code population (error-handling criterion: silent lookup miss, unchecked subprocess returncode, pgrep self-match, invisible best-effort check failure).

The fail-open detection language litmus is: name every world in which the check produces any definite result (pass or fail); if 'producer never ran', 'instrument received wrong input', or 'producer emitted nothing' is among them, the check cannot distinguish verdict from its own failure.

Live calibration via eval_solver.run_case must demonstrate 9/9 pre-fix seeded cases fire findings naming the fail-open defect and 9/9 post-fix cases yield zero findings (with fallback protocol for incidental defects or genuine liveness gaps in the seeded fix).

Author guide documentation at 'rebar explain review' must present the fail-open pattern with two worked examples (one test-oracle, one shipped-code) to satisfy AC since fail-open language lands in existing criteria with no per-criterion explain surface.
